Theme

Latin word

exemplum

exemplum, exemplī n.

noun, second declension

an example, an instance; a model to follow; example (to follow or to avoid)

In this lexicon

  • example

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Phil. 13.2: exemplī causā paucōs nōmināvī; Traupman 146: exemplum praebet

  • model

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 6.5: breve et efficāx per exempla; Tac. Germ. 7.1: ducēs exemplō potius quam imperiō

  • exemplum mittere: forward

    classical

Examples

  • longum iter est per praecepta, breve et efficāx per exempla

    the road through rules is long; through examples it is short and effectiveSen. Ep. 6.5

    In the entry for example

  • ducēs exemplō potius quam imperiō, sī prōmptī, sī cōnspicuī, sī ante aciem agant, admīrātiōne praesunt

    leaders lead by example rather than by command: if they are ready, if they are seen, if they fight in front, they lead because they are admiredTac. Germ. 7.1

    In the entry for example

  • exemplī causā paucōs nōmināvī

    I have named a few, by way of exampleCic. Phil. 13.2

    In the entry for example

  • īnspicere tamquam in speculum in vītās omnium jubeō, atque ex aliīs sūmere exemplum sibi

    I tell him to look into everyone’s life as into a mirror, and to take from others a model for himselfTer. Ad. 415–416
